source_preamble.text_exact:
GPIO Output Controller — self-authored small embedded task

Scope: two independent logical LEDs on a host-observable GPIO platform. This is a newly authored task, not a new open-source project. Implement the fixed C11 API. Do not provide a main function or implement platform callbacks.
source_preamble.role: original scope context; no additional score items

review_protocol.unit: One original numbered requirement, unchanged; every stated condition belongs to this single judgment.
review_protocol.pass: P: the unchanged candidate code provides direct, internally consistent evidence that every condition in this whole numbered requirement is implemented within the declared input and platform contract.
review_protocol.fail: F: code directly contradicts, omits, or fails to implement at least one required condition. Do not invent a missing function or repair a behavior before judging.
review_protocol.uncertain: U: evidence is insufficient to decide the whole requirement, including an unresolved path, external behavior beyond the declared platform contract, or code whose meaning cannot be determined reliably.
review_protocol.not_applicable: N/A: a stated contract/scope condition makes the entire numbered requirement inapplicable. Cite the exact scope basis. Missing code, a missing feature, compilation failure, or reviewer difficulty is not an applicability reason.
review_protocol.compound_requirement: P only if all conjunctive conditions hold; an established violation of any condition makes the whole item F; otherwise unresolved conditions make it U. Never split a numbered item or award partial credit.
required_evidence: Exact candidate identity and code-file SHA256 bindings
Relevant code file and line spans, or precise missing evidence
Short reason covering all conditions; N/A must additionally cite contract scope
review_protocol.build_errors: Review the original candidate without editing. Pure syntax/build obstacles do not automatically make functional requirements F; assess recoverable intended semantics only where the original code provides unambiguous evidence, otherwise U. Do not assume missing functional behavior.
review_protocol.host_separation: Existing Host scenarios are a separately bound executable protocol. Their verdicts must not be copied into static judgments or used as a substitute for code evidence.
review_protocol.support_formula: P/(P+F+U); N/A excluded with count and rationale retained. Report P/F/U/N/A and the denominator. An unreviewed or absent candidate has no fabricated item verdicts.
review_protocol.no_protocol_equivalence: These are new-task whole numbered-requirement judgments. They are not the same units as the legacy Crazyflie/OnStep/DiscoBot 100/90/124 static testcase sets or the separate atomic-requirement coverage protocol.

host_protocol_binding.meaning: Binding and requirement-to-scenario links only; this preparation creates no executable or static outcomes.

items.requirement_original_text: GO-R01 Initialization: gpio_output_init() configures logical state for channels 0 and 1 as off and calls board_gpio_write(0, false), then board_gpio_write(1, false), exactly once each. Reinitialization has the same effects regardless of prior state.
GO-R02 Before the first initialization, set, toggle, and get return false and cause no platform writes; get does not modify the caller's output variable.

GO-R03 Valid set: after initialization, gpio_output_set(channel, on) for channel 0 or 1 returns true, stores exactly the requested Boolean state, and calls board_gpio_write exactly once with that channel and value, even if the value is unchanged.
GO-R04 Channel independence: changing a valid channel leaves the other channel's stored state unchanged and never writes the other channel.
GO-R05 Valid toggle: after initialization, gpio_output_toggle(channel) negates the stored state of the requested channel, makes exactly one matching platform write, and returns true.
GO-R06 Invalid channels: any uint8_t channel other than 0 or 1 makes set, toggle, and get return false, with no state changes or platform writes. Failed get leaves its output variable unchanged.

GO-R07 Query: after initialization, gpio_output_get(channel, out_on) for a valid channel and non-null pointer returns true and writes its current state to out_on. Query never writes GPIO or changes controller state.
GO-R08 Null output: gpio_output_get(channel, NULL) returns false and has no side effects.
